Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy air-space opacities that are predominantly distributed in the middle and lower pulmonary fields. This pattern of bilateral mid-to-lower zone consolidation is a recognized radiographic presentation of amiodarone-induced pneumonitis, distinguishing it from unilateral or strictly upper-lobe predominant processes.
